extracted.intended_audience: prospective postdoctoral fellows (and their mentors) seeking JCC postdoctoral fellowships in biomedical research
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and program standards for applicants to the Jane Coffin Childs three-year postdoctoral fellowships supporting fundamental biomedical research. Describes mission focus, selection process, stipend/support details, expectations of fellows, and program commitments to mentoring and inclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: support fundamental scientific research advancing understanding of human disease
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund’s mission has broadened to support fundamental scientific research that advances understanding of the causes, treatments, and cures for human disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originally inspired to support cancer research; the Fund supports basic cancer and human disease–related research. Applicants should propose fundamental biomedical research that advances human health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship target: best and brightest postdoctoral fellows
rubrics_metrics.description: The JCC Fund provides three years of salary support to the best and brightest postdoctoral fellows, as selected by the esteemed Board of Scientific Advisors (BSA), pursuing fundamental biomedical research to advance human health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to be at the postdoctoral level and of high caliber; historically the Fund has awarded over 1,800 fellows and grantees working in laboratories worldwide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection standard: rigorous review by the Board of Scientific Advisors (BSA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rigorous selection process, the mentoring and sharing of knowledge that the BSA provides each year is one of the great strengths of the JCC Fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are evaluated by an eminent BSA (which has included Nobel laureates and other distinguished scientists). Competition is high (each year over ~350 applications are received), and the BSA’s judgment is central to award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration and stipend/support levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Three years of salary support. The 2026 fellowship stipend levels are Year 1 $72,000; Year 2 $74,000 and Year 3 $76,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to salary/stipend, fellows receive additional funding for research costs, travel costs, relocation costs, supplemented salaries for fellows with dependents, and access to additional child care funds provided by a donor gift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual number of awards and funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The JCC Fund supports between twenty-five and thirty new three-year postdoctoral fellows each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most fellowships are funded from the JCC Fund endowment; annually 10–13 fellowships are funded by corporate and non-profit partners (e.g., Merck, HHMI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellow expectations: participation in annual symposium and professional development
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year the BSA and the currently funded fellows are expected to attend an annual symposium where fellows will partake in poster sessions, scientific sessions and career development sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendance and active participation are expected to enhance networking, communication, and scientific skills; the Fund emphasizes clear, accessible scientific communication among researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to mentoring and inclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The JCC Fund is committed to mentoring and advancing people from all backgrounds and... is dedicated to increasing the inclusivity of the scientific workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentoring and knowledge-sharing from the BSA are program strengths; applicants and host labs should be prepared to engage in mentoring and inclusive practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic scope of supported research placements
rubrics_metrics.description: Jane Coffin Childs Fellows and grantees have been awarded to conduct research in laboratories in North America, Europe, Japan and Australia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program funds fellows working internationally in major research regions; prospective applicants may be based or intend to work in these geographic areas.
